Statement I: The arguments of trigonometric, logarithmic, and exponential functions appearing in physical equations must be dimensionless.

Statement II: Physical quantities having different dimensions can be added or subtracted provided they are measured in the same system of units.

In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: भौतिक समीकरणों में आने वाले त्रिकोणमितीय, लघुगणकीय और चरघातांकी फलनों के कोणांक (तर्क) विमाहीन होने चाहिए।

कथन II: विभिन्न विमाओं वाली भौतिक राशियों को जोड़ा या घटाया जा सकता है, बशर्ते उन्हें एक ही मात्रक प्रणाली में मापा गया हो।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Statement I
Functions such as \(\sin(\theta)\), \(\ln(x)\), and \(e^x\) can be expanded into infinite series involving sums of powers of the argument (e.g., \(1 + x + x^2/2! + \ldots\)). If the argument \(x\) had dimensions, terms with different powers of dimensions would be added together, violating the fundamental principle of homogeneity. Thus, arguments of all transcendental functions must be dimensionless numbers. Statement I is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement II
The principle of homogeneity strictly forbids the addition or subtraction of physical quantities that have different dimensions, regardless of the system of units used. For example, a velocity (\([\text{L}\text{T}^{-1}]\)) can never be added to a force (\([\text{M}\text{L}\text{T}^{-2}]\)), even if both are expressed in SI units. Statement II is completely incorrect.

Step 3: Conclusion
Statement I accurately describes the required dimensionless nature of transcendental function arguments, while Statement II violates the foundational principle of dimensional homogeneity.

Final Conceptual Conclusion: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

चरण 1: कथन I का मूल्यांकन
\(\sin(\theta)\), \(\ln(x)\), और \(e^x\) जैसे फलनों को कोणांक की घातों के योग वाली अनंत श्रेणियों (उदा. \(1 + x + x^2/2! + \ldots\)) में विस्तारित किया जा सकता है। यदि कोणांक \(x\) की कोई विमा होती, तो विभिन्न विमीय घातों वाले पदों को एक साथ जोड़ना पड़ता, जो समांगता के मूलभूत सिद्धांत का उल्लंघन करता है। अतः सभी अबीजीय फलनों के कोणांक विमाहीन संख्याएँ होने चाहिए। कथन I सही है।

चरण 2: कथन II का मूल्यांकन
समांगता का सिद्धांत विभिन्न विमाओं वाली भौतिक राशियों को जोड़ने या घटाने पर पूर्ण प्रतिबंध लगाता है, चाहे किसी भी मात्रक प्रणाली का उपयोग किया गया हो। उदाहरण के लिए, वेग (\([\text{L}\text{T}^{-1}]\)) को बल (\([\text{M}\text{L}\text{T}^{-2}]\)) में कभी नहीं जोड़ा जा सकता, भले ही दोनों SI मात्रकों में व्यक्त किए गए हों। कथन II पूर्णतः गलत है।

चरण 3: निष्कर्ष
कथन I अबीजीय फलन कोणांकों की विमाहीन प्रकृति का सटीक वर्णन करता है, जबकि कथन II विमीय समांगता के मूलभूत सिद्धांत का उल्लंघन करता है।

अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक निष्कर्ष: कथन I सही है लेकिन कथन II गलत है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITSANDMEASUREMENT_ST3_Q01 - Analysis of base units and supplementary units

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: In the International System of Units (SI), there are exactly seven base units.

Statement II: Plane angle and solid angle have units of radian and steradian respectively, but both are dimensionless quantities.

Statement III: The candela is the SI base unit of luminous intensity.

In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मात्रक प्रणाली (SI) में ठीक सात मूल मात्रक हैं।

कथन II: समतल कोण और ठोस कोण के मात्रक क्रमशः रेडियन और स्टेरेडियन हैं, लेकिन दोनों विमाहीन राशियाँ हैं।

कथन III: कैन्डेला ज्योति तीव्रता का SI मूल मात्रक है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Statement I
The SI system is built upon seven fundamental base quantities and their respective units: metre (length), kilogram (mass), second (time), ampere (electric current), kelvin (thermodynamic temperature), mole (amount of substance), and candela (luminous intensity). Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement II
Plane angle is defined as the ratio of arc length to radius (\([\text{L}]/[\text{L}]\)) with SI unit radian (\(\text{rad}\)), and solid angle is defined as the ratio of intercepted area to the square of radius (\([\text{L}^2]/[\text{L}^2]\)) with SI unit steradian (\(\text{sr}\)). Both are pure ratios with dimension \([\text{M}^0\text{L}^0\text{T}^0]\). Therefore, Statement II is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement III
As defined in Table 1.1 of the NCERT textbook, the candela (symbol \(\text{cd}\)) is the SI base unit of luminous intensity in a given direction. Therefore, Statement III is correct.

Step 4: Conclusion
All three statements I, II, and III are scientifically accurate and consistent with the SI definitions.

Final Conceptual Conclusion: Statements I, II, and III are all correct.

चरण 1: कथन I का मूल्यांकन
SI प्रणाली सात मूलभूत मूल राशियों और उनके संबंधित मात्रकों पर आधारित है: मीटर (लंबाई), किलोग्राम (द्रव्यमान), सेकंड (समय), ऐम्पियर (विद्युत धारा), केल्विन (ऊष्मागतिक ताप), मोल (पदार्थ की मात्रा), और कैन्डेला (ज्योति तीव्रता)। अतः कथन I सही है।

चरण 2: कथन II का मूल्यांकन
समतल कोण को चाप की लंबाई और त्रिज्या के अनुपात (\([\text{L}]/[\text{L}]\)) के रूप में परिभाषित किया जाता है जिसका मात्रक रेडियन (\(\text{rad}\)) है, तथा ठोस कोण को परिबद्ध क्षेत्रफल और त्रिज्या के वर्ग के अनुपात (\([\text{L}^2]/[\text{L}^2]\)) के रूप में परिभाषित किया जाता है जिसका मात्रक स्टेरेडियन (\(\text{sr}\)) है। दोनों शुद्ध अनुपात हैं जिनकी विमा \([\text{M}^0\text{L}^0\text{T}^0]\) है। अतः कथन II सही है।

चरण 3: कथन III का मूल्यांकन
NCERT पाठ्यपुस्तक की सारणी 1.1 में दी गई परिभाषा के अनुसार, कैन्डेला (प्रतीक \(\text{cd}\)) किसी दी गई दिशा में ज्योति तीव्रता का SI मूल मात्रक है। अतः कथन III सही है।

चरण 4: निष्कर्ष
कथन I, II और III तीनों वैज्ञानिक रूप से सही हैं और SI परिभाषाओं के अनुरूप हैं।

अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक निष्कर्ष: कथन I, II और III सभी सही हैं।

answer.text: Statements I, II, and III are all correct.
Statement I and II are correct, but Statement III is incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statements II and III are incorrect.
Statement II and III are correct, but Statement I is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITSANDMEASUREMENT_ST3_Q02 - Rules for identifying significant figures in measurements

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: All non-zero digits and all zeroes appearing between two non-zero digits are significant.

Statement II: In a number without a decimal point, trailing zeroes are always significant.

Statement III: A choice of change of units does not change the number of significant figures in a measurement.

In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: सभी गैर-शून्य अंक और दो गैर-शून्य अंकों के बीच आने वाले सभी शून्य सार्थक होते हैं।

कथन II: दशमलव बिंदु रहित किसी संख्या में अनुगामी शून्य सदैव सार्थक होते हैं।

कथन III: मात्रकों को बदलने से किसी मापन में सार्थक अंकों की संख्या नहीं बदलती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Statement I
According to the fundamental rules of significant figures, all non-zero digits are significant, and any zero lying between two non-zero digits is significant regardless of the decimal point position (e.g., in \(2005\) or \(2.005\), all four digits are significant). Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement II
In an integer without a decimal point, trailing or terminal zeroes are not significant because they merely indicate the scale or magnitude (e.g., \(12300\text{ m}\) has only three significant figures). Therefore, Statement II is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement III
Significant figures reflect the precision of the measuring instrument and cannot be altered by rewriting the measurement in another unit (e.g., \(2.308\text{ m} = 230.8\text{ cm} = 0.002308\text{ km}\); all have four significant figures). Therefore, Statement III is correct.

Step 4: Conclusion
Statements I and III are correct, while Statement II is incorrect.

Final Conceptual Conclusion: Statements I and III are correct, but Statement II is incorrect.

चरण 1: कथन I का मूल्यांकन
सार्थक अंकों के मूलभूत नियमों के अनुसार, सभी गैर-शून्य अंक सार्थक होते हैं, और दो गैर-शून्य अंकों के बीच स्थित कोई भी शून्य सार्थक होता है, चाहे दशमलव बिंदु कहीं भी हो (उदा. \(2005\) या \(2.005\) में सभी चार अंक सार्थक हैं)। अतः कथन I सही है।

चरण 2: कथन II का मूल्यांकन
दशमलव बिंदु रहित पूर्णांक में, अनुगामी या अंतिम शून्य सार्थक नहीं होते हैं क्योंकि वे केवल परिमाण के पैमाने को दर्शाते हैं (उदा. \(12300\text{ m}\) में केवल तीन सार्थक अंक हैं)। अतः कथन II गलत है।

चरण 3: कथन III का मूल्यांकन
सार्थक अंक मापक यंत्र की परिशुद्धता को दर्शाते हैं और मापन को किसी अन्य मात्रक में लिखने से नहीं बदलते हैं (उदा. \(2.308\text{ m} = 230.8\text{ cm} = 0.002308\text{ km}\); सभी में चार सार्थक अंक हैं)। अतः कथन III सही है।

चरण 4: निष्कर्ष
कथन I और III सही हैं, जबकि कथन II गलत है।

अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक निष्कर्ष: कथन I और III सही हैं, लेकिन कथन II गलत है।

answer.text: Statements I, II, and III are all correct.
Statements I and III are correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statements I and II are correct, but Statement III is incorrect.
Statement II is correct, but Statements I and III are incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITSANDMEASUREMENT_ST3_Q03 - Significant figures in arithmetic and exact numbers

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: In multiplication or division, the final result should retain as many significant figures as are present in the original measured quantity with the least significant figures.

Statement II: In addition or subtraction, the final result should retain as many significant figures as are present in the original measured quantity with the least significant figures.

Statement III: Exact numbers appearing in physical formulas, such as the factor \(2\) in the perimeter formula \(s = 2\pi r\), possess an infinite number of significant figures.

In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: गुणा या भाग में, अंतिम परिणाम में केवल उतने ही सार्थक अंक होने चाहिए जितने कि न्यूनतम सार्थक अंकों वाली मूल मापी गई राशि में उपस्थित हैं।

कथन II: जोड़ या घटाव में, अंतिम परिणाम में केवल उतने ही सार्थक अंक होने चाहिए जितने कि न्यूनतम सार्थक अंकों वाली मूल मापी गई राशि में उपस्थित हैं।

कथन III: भौतिक सूत्रों में आने वाली यथार्थ संख्याएँ, जैसे परिधि सूत्र \(s = 2\pi r\) में गुणक \(2\), अनंत सार्थक अंक रखती हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Statement I
In multiplication or division, the rule requires that the final computed value retains only as many significant figures as the least precise input factor. For example, dividing \(4.237\text{ g}\) (four significant figures) by \(2.51\text{ cm}^3\) (three significant figures) yields \(1.69\text{ g cm}^{-3}\) (three significant figures). Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement II
In addition or subtraction, the precision of the result is governed by decimal places, not significant figures. The final answer must retain only as many decimal places as the number having the fewest decimal places. Therefore, Statement II is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement III
Exact numbers and pure counting integers (such as \(2\) in \(s = 2\pi r\) or \(1/2\) in \(E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2\)) have no experimental uncertainty and can be regarded as having an infinite number of significant figures (\(2.0, 2.00, 2.000\ldots\)). Therefore, Statement III is correct.

Step 4: Conclusion
Statements I and III are correct, whereas Statement II is incorrect.

Final Conceptual Conclusion: Statements I and III are correct, but Statement II is incorrect.

चरण 1: कथन I का मूल्यांकन
गुणा या भाग में, नियम यह निर्धारित करता है कि अंतिम परिकलित मान में केवल उतने ही सार्थक अंक होने चाहिए जितने कि न्यूनतम परिशुद्ध इनपुट कारक में हैं। उदाहरण के लिए, \(4.237\text{ g}\) (चार सार्थक अंक) को \(2.51\text{ cm}^3\) (तीन सार्थक अंक) से विभाजित करने पर \(1.69\text{ g cm}^{-3}\) (तीन सार्थक अंक) प्राप्त होता है। अतः कथन I सही है।

चरण 2: कथन II का मूल्यांकन
जोड़ या घटाव में, परिणाम की परिशुद्धता सार्थक अंकों द्वारा नहीं बल्कि दशमलव स्थानों द्वारा निर्धारित होती है। अंतिम परिणाम में केवल उतने ही दशमलव स्थान होने चाहिए जितने कि न्यूनतम दशमलव स्थानों वाली संख्या में हैं। अतः कथन II गलत है।

चरण 3: कथन III का मूल्यांकन
यथार्थ संख्याएँ और विशुद्ध गणना पूर्णांक (जैसे \(s = 2\pi r\) में \(2\) या \(E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2\) में \(1/2\)) में कोई प्रायोगिक अनिश्चितता नहीं होती है और इन्हें अनंत सार्थक अंक (\(2.0, 2.00, 2.000\ldots\)) रखने वाला माना जा सकता है। अतः कथन III सही है।

चरण 4: निष्कर्ष
कथन I और III सही हैं, जबकि कथन II गलत है।

अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक निष्कर्ष: कथन I और III सही हैं, लेकिन कथन II गलत है।

answer.text: Statements I, II, and III are all correct.
Statements I and II are correct, but Statement III is incorrect.
Statements I and III are correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement II is correct, but Statements I and III are incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITSANDMEASUREMENT_ST3_Q04 - Scope and limitations of dimensional analysis

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: If a physical equation is dimensionally inconsistent, it must be physically wrong.

Statement II: The method of dimensions can determine the numerical value of dimensionless proportionality constants appearing in derived physical formulas.

Statement III: The arguments of trigonometric, logarithmic, and exponential functions appearing in physical equations must be dimensionless.

In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: यदि कोई भौतिक समीकरण विमीय रूप से असंगत है, तो वह निश्चित रूप से भौतिक रूप से गलत होता है।

कथन II: विमीय विधि व्युत्पन्न भौतिक सूत्रों में आने वाले विमाहीन आनुपातिकता नियतांकों के संख्यात्मक मान को निर्धारित कर सकती है।

कथन III: भौतिक समीकरणों में आने वाले त्रिकोणमितीय, लघुगणकीय और चरघातांकी फलनों के कोणांक (तर्क) विमाहीन होने चाहिए।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Statement I
According to the principle of homogeneity of dimensions, every physically valid equation must balance dimensionally across all additive terms. If an equation fails this consistency test, it is definitively proven wrong. Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement II
Dimensional analysis is inherently incapable of determining dimensionless proportionality constants (e.g., the factor \(2\pi\) in \(T = 2\pi \sqrt{l/g}\) or \(1/2\) in \(E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2\)) because dimensionless numbers have zero powers for all base dimensions (\([\text{M}^0\text{L}^0\text{T}^0]\)). These constants must be evaluated through experimental measurement or complete mathematical integration. Therefore, Statement II is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement III
Special mathematical functions such as \(\sin(x)\), \(\cos(x)\), \(\ln(x)\), and \(e^x\) can be expanded into infinite power series. If the argument \(x\) carried a physical dimension, terms of different dimensions would be added together, violating the principle of homogeneity. Hence, arguments of all transcendental functions must be dimensionless. Therefore, Statement III is correct.

Step 4: Conclusion
Statements I and III are correct, while Statement II is incorrect.

Final Conceptual Conclusion: Statements I and III are correct, but Statement II is incorrect.

चरण 1: कथन I का मूल्यांकन
विमाओं की समांगता के सिद्धांत के अनुसार, प्रत्येक भौतिक रूप से मान्य समीकरण को सभी योज्य पदों में विमीय रूप से संतुलित होना चाहिए। यदि कोई समीकरण इस संगतता परीक्षण में विफल रहता है, तो वह निश्चित रूप से गलत सिद्ध होता है। अतः कथन I सही है।

चरण 2: कथन II का मूल्यांकन
विमीय विश्लेषण स्वाभाविक रूप से विमाहीन आनुपातिकता नियतांकों (जैसे \(T = 2\pi \sqrt{l/g}\) में \(2\pi\) या \(E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2\) में \(1/2\)) का निर्धारण करने में असमर्थ है क्योंकि विमाहीन संख्याओं में सभी मूल विमाओं की घातें शून्य (\([\text{M}^0\text{L}^0\text{T}^0]\)) होती हैं। इन नियतांकों का मूल्यांकन प्रायोगिक मापन या पूर्ण गणितीय समाकलन द्वारा किया जाना चाहिए। अतः कथन II गलत है।

चरण 3: कथन III का मूल्यांकन
विशिष्ट गणितीय फलन जैसे \(\sin(x)\), \(\cos(x)\), \(\ln(x)\), और \(e^x\) को अनंत घात श्रेणियों में विस्तारित किया जा सकता है। यदि कोणांक \(x\) की कोई भौतिक विमा होती, तो विभिन्न विमाओं वाले पदों को एक साथ जोड़ना पड़ता, जो समांगता के सिद्धांत का उल्लंघन करता है। अतः सभी अबीजीय फलनों के कोणांक विमाहीन होने चाहिए। अतः कथन III सही है।

चरण 4: निष्कर्ष
कथन I और III सही हैं, जबकि कथन II गलत है।

अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक निष्कर्ष: कथन I और III सही हैं, लेकिन कथन II गलत है।

answer.text: Statements I, II, and III are all correct.
Statements I and II are correct, but Statement III is incorrect.
Statement II and III are correct, but Statement I is incorrect.
Statements I and III are correct, but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MATCHLIST_Q01 - SI base quantities and their base units

questiontext.text:
Match List I (SI Base Quantity) with List II (SI Base Unit):

List I List II
A. Electric currentI. kelvin
B. Thermodynamic temperatureII. mole
C. Amount of substanceIII. candela
D. Luminous intensityIV. ampere

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identification of the unit of electric current
Electric current is an SI base quantity defined with the base unit ampere (symbol: \(\text{A}\)).

Step 2: Identification of the unit of thermodynamic temperature
Thermodynamic temperature is an SI base quantity defined with the base unit kelvin (symbol: \(\text{K}\)).

Step 3: Identification of the unit of amount of substance
Amount of substance is an SI base quantity containing elementary entities, defined with the base unit mole (symbol: \(\text{mol}\)).

Step 4: Identification of the unit of luminous intensity
Luminous intensity is an SI base quantity defined with the base unit candela (symbol: \(\text{cd}\)).

Step 5: Correct matching combination
The correct correspondence pairs electric current with ampere, thermodynamic temperature with kelvin, amount of substance with mole, and luminous intensity with candela.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MATCHLIST_Q02 - Units retained for general use and SI equivalents

questiontext.text:
Match List I (Unit retained for general use) with List II (Value in SI unit):

List I List II
A. 1 quintalI. \(10^{-3}\text{ m}^3\)
B. 1 hectareII. \(10^2\text{ kg}\)
C. 1 barIII. \(10^4\text{ m}^2\)
D. 1 litreIV. \(10^5\text{ Pa}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: SI equivalent of quintal
A quintal is a metric unit of mass retained for general use and equals \(100\text{ kg} = 10^2\text{ kg}\).

Step 2: SI equivalent of hectare
A hectare is a unit of land area equal to the area of a square with sides of \(1\text{ hm} = 100\text{ m}\), giving \((100\text{ m})^2 = 10^4\text{ m}^2\).

Step 3: SI equivalent of bar
The bar is a metric unit of pressure defined as \(0.1\text{ MPa} = 10^5\text{ Pa}\).

Step 4: SI equivalent of litre
The litre is a unit of volume equal to one cubic decimetre: \(1\text{ dm}^3 = (10^{-1}\text{ m})^3 = 10^{-3}\text{ m}^3\).

Step 5: Correct matching combination
The correct correspondence pairs quintal with \(10^2\text{ kg}\), hectare with \(10^4\text{ m}^2\), bar with \(10^5\text{ Pa}\), and litre with \(10^{-3}\text{ m}^3\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MATCHLIST_Q03 - Number of significant figures in measured values

questiontext.text:
Match List I (Measured value) with List II (Number of significant figures):

List I List II
A. \(0.005\text{ m}\)I. 3
B. \(4.8\text{ g cm}^{-3}\)II. 1
C. \(2.64 \times 10^{24}\text{ kg}\)III. 4
D. \(0.2370\text{ g cm}^{-3}\)IV. 2

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Significant figures in \(0.005\text{ m}\)
For a number less than \(1\), zeros to the right of the decimal point but to the left of the first non-zero digit are not significant. Only the non-zero digit \(5\) is significant, giving \(1\) significant figure.

Step 2: Significant figures in \(4.8\text{ g cm}^{-3}\)
All non-zero digits are significant. The digits \(4\) and \(8\) are both significant, giving \(2\) significant figures.

Step 3: Significant figures in \(2.64 \times 10^{24}\text{ kg}\)
In scientific notation, the power of \(10\) is irrelevant to the count of significant figures; all digits in the base number are significant. The digits \(2, 6, 4\) yield \(3\) significant figures.

Step 4: Significant figures in \(0.2370\text{ g cm}^{-3}\)
The leading zero before the decimal is not significant. The digits \(2, 3, 7\) are significant, and trailing zeros in a number with a decimal point are significant. Thus, the four digits \(2, 3, 7, 0\) give \(4\) significant figures.

Step 5: Correct matching combination
The correct correspondence pairs \(0.005\text{ m}\) with \(1\) significant figure, \(4.8\text{ g cm}^{-3}\) with \(2\) significant figures, \(2.64 \times 10^{24}\text{ kg}\) with \(3\) significant figures, and \(0.2370\text{ g cm}^{-3}\) with \(4\) significant figures.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MATCHLIST_Q04 - Dimensional formulae of physical quantities

questiontext.text:
Match List I (Physical quantity) with List II (Dimensional formula):

List I List II
A. Universal gravitational constant (\(G\))I. \([\text{M L}^2\text{T}^{-1}]\)
B. Planck constant (\(h\))II. \([\text{M}^{-1}\text{L}^3\text{T}^{-2}]\)
C. ForceIII. \([\text{M L}\text{T}^{-2}]\)
D. Kinetic energyIV. \([\text{M L}^2\text{T}^{-2}]\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Dimensional formula of universal gravitational constant
From Newton's law of gravitation, \(F = G\frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2}\), so \(G = \frac{F r^2}{m_1 m_2}\). Substituting dimensions gives \([G] = \frac{[\text{M L T}^{-2}][\text{L}^2]}{[\text{M}][\text{M}]} = [\text{M}^{-1}\text{L}^3\text{T}^{-2}]\).

Step 2: Dimensional formula of Planck constant
From the energy relation \(E = h \nu\), the Planck constant is \(h = \frac{E}{\nu}\). Substituting dimensions gives \([h] = \frac{[\text{M L}^2\text{T}^{-2}]}{[\text{T}^{-1}]} = [\text{M L}^2\text{T}^{-1}]\).

Step 3: Dimensional formula of force
Force is mass times acceleration: \([F] = [\text{M}][\text{L T}^{-2}] = [\text{M L T}^{-2}]\).

Step 4: Dimensional formula of kinetic energy
Kinetic energy is given by \(K = \frac{1}{2}m v^2\). Substituting dimensions gives \([K] = [\text{M}][\text{L T}^{-1}]^2 = [\text{M L}^2\text{T}^{-2}]\).

Step 5: Correct matching combination
The correct correspondence pairs the universal gravitational constant with \([\text{M}^{-1}\text{L}^3\text{T}^{-2}]\), the Planck constant with \([\text{M L}^2\text{T}^{-1}]\), force with \([\text{M L T}^{-2}]\), and kinetic energy with \([\text{M L}^2\text{T}^{-2}]\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q01 - Volume conversion of cube into cubic metres

questiontext.text: A small cube has a side length of \( 1\text{ cm} \). What is the volume of this cube expressed in cubic metres (\( \text{m}^3 \))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Side length of the cube: \( l = 1\text{ cm} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Unit Definitions
The relationship between centimetre and metre is: \[ 1\text{ cm} = 10^{-2}\text{ m} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
The volume \( V \) of a cube of side \( l \) is: \[ V = l^3 \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the length in metres: \[ V = (1\text{ cm})^3 = (10^{-2}\text{ m})^3 = 10^{-6}\text{ m}^3 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( (\text{m})^3 = \text{m}^3 \). The volume of the cube is \( 10^{-6}\text{ m}^3 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q02 - Distance covered per second from vehicle speed

questiontext.text: A vehicle is travelling at a uniform speed of \( 18\text{ km h}^{-1} \). What distance does it cover in \( 1\text{ s} \)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Speed of vehicle: \( v = 18\text{ km h}^{-1} \).
Time elapsed: \( t = 1\text{ s} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Unit Conversions
Convert speed from kilometres per hour to metres per second using: \[ 1\text{ km h}^{-1} = \frac{1000\text{ m}}{3600\text{ s}} = \frac{5}{18}\text{ m s}^{-1} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Distance covered under uniform motion is given by: \[ d = v \times t \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Convert the speed: \[ v = 18 \times \frac{5}{18}\text{ m s}^{-1} = 5\text{ m s}^{-1} \] Calculate distance covered in \( 1\text{ s} \): \[ d = 5\text{ m s}^{-1} \times 1\text{ s} = 5\text{ m} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units check: \( \text{m s}^{-1} \times \text{s} = \text{m} \). The distance covered is \( 5\text{ m} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q03 - Mass conversion from carat units into grams

questiontext.text: A gemstone has a measured mass of \( 15\text{ carats} \). What is the mass of this gemstone expressed in grams?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of gemstone: \( m = 15\text{ c} \) (carats).

Step 2: Assumptions and Unit Definitions
By standard unit definition retained for general use: \[ 1\text{ carat} = 200\text{ mg} = 0.200\text{ g} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Total mass in grams: \[ m(\text{g}) = m(\text{carats}) \times 0.200\text{ g/carat} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Multiply the number of carats by the mass per carat: \[ m = 15 \times 0.200\text{ g} = 3.0\text{ g} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( \text{carat} \times \frac{\text{g}}{\text{carat}} = \text{g} \). The mass of the gemstone is \( 3.0\text{ g} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q04 - Energy conversion between SI and CGS units

questiontext.text: Convert \( 1\text{ kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-2} \) (which equals \( 1\text{ J} \)) into the corresponding CGS unit \( \text{g cm}^2\text{ s}^{-2} \).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Quantity to convert: \( 1\text{ kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-2} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Base Unit Conversions
The conversion factors between SI and CGS base units are: \[ 1\text{ kg} = 10^3\text{ g} \] \[ 1\text{ m} = 10^2\text{ cm} \implies 1\text{ m}^2 = (10^2\text{ cm})^2 = 10^4\text{ cm}^2 \] \[ 1\text{ s} = 1\text{ s} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Substitute the converted base units into the expression: \[ 1\text{ kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-2} = (10^3\text{ g}) \times (10^4\text{ cm}^2) \times (1\text{ s}^{-2}) \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Combine the powers of 10: \[ 10^3 \times 10^4 = 10^{3+4} = 10^7 \] Hence: \[ 1\text{ kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-2} = 10^7\text{ g cm}^2\text{ s}^{-2} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking dimensions: mass \( \times \) length\(^2 \times \) time\(^{-2}\). The converted value is \( 10^7\text{ g cm}^2\text{ s}^{-2} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q05 - Volume conversion from litres to cubic metres

questiontext.text: A chemical container holds \( 4.5\text{ L} \) of solution. What is this volume in SI base units (\( \text{m}^3 \))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Volume: \( V = 4.5\text{ L} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Unit Definitions
By standard definition of the litre: \[ 1\text{ L} = 1\text{ dm}^3 = (10^{-1}\text{ m})^3 = 10^{-3}\text{ m}^3 \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Volume in cubic metres: \[ V(\text{m}^3) = V(\text{L}) \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^3\text{ L}^{-1} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given volume: \[ V = 4.5 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^3 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units check: \( \text{L} \times \frac{\text{m}^3}{\text{L}} = \text{m}^3 \). The volume is \( 4.5 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^3 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q06 - Total seconds calculation in one full day

questiontext.text: Calculate the total number of seconds contained in exactly one standard solar day (\( 1\text{ d} = 24\text{ h} \)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Time interval: \( t = 1\text{ day} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Unit Relationships
The conversion chain from day to seconds is: \[ 1\text{ day} = 24\text{ hours} \] \[ 1\text{ hour} = 60\text{ minutes} \] \[ 1\text{ minute} = 60\text{ seconds} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ t(\text{s}) = 1\text{ d} \times 24\frac{\text{h}}{\text{d}} \times 60\frac{\text{min}}{\text{h}} \times 60\frac{\text{s}}{\text{min}} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Multiply the conversion factors: \[ t = 24 \times 3600\text{ s} = 86400\text{ s} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: days cancel, hours cancel, minutes cancel, leaving seconds. Exactly \( 86400\text{ s} \) are in one day.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q07 - Plane angle calculation from arc and radius

questiontext.text: An arc of length \( \mathrm{d}s = 15\text{ cm} \) subtends a plane angle \( \mathrm{d}\theta \) at the centre of a circle of radius \( r = 50\text{ cm} \). What is the value of \( \mathrm{d}\theta \) in radians?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Arc length: \( \mathrm{d}s = 15\text{ cm} \).
Radius of circle: \( r = 50\text{ cm} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Definitions
Plane angle in radians is defined as the ratio of arc length to radius: \[ \mathrm{d}\theta = \frac{\mathrm{d}s}{r} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Ensure both lengths are expressed in the same units before dividing.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values: \[ \mathrm{d}\theta = \frac{15\text{ cm}}{50\text{ cm}} = 0.30\text{ rad} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The ratio is dimensionless, giving the unit radian (\( \text{rad} \)). The angle is \( 0.30\text{ rad} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q08 - Density calculation with significant figures retention

questiontext.text: A solid substance having a mass of \( 5.74\text{ g} \) occupies a volume of \( 1.2\text{ cm}^3 \). Calculate the density of the substance to the appropriate number of significant figures.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass: \( m = 5.74\text{ g} \) (3 significant figures).
Volume: \( V = 1.2\text{ cm}^3 \) (2 significant figures).

Step 2: Rules for Significant Figures in Division
In multiplication and division, the final result must retain as many significant figures as the input measurement with the least number of significant figures (here, 2 significant figures from volume).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Density: \[ \rho = \frac{m}{V} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Divide mass by volume: \[ \rho = \frac{5.74}{1.2}\text{ g cm}^{-3} = 4.78333\dots\text{ g cm}^{-3} \] Rounding to 2 significant figures (since the next digit is 8, raise 7 to 8): \[ \rho = 4.8\text{ g cm}^{-3} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The result retains 2 significant figures. The reported density is \( 4.8\text{ g cm}^{-3} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q09 - Sum of masses adhering to decimal precision

questiontext.text: Three separate masses are measured as \( 436.32\text{ g} \), \( 227.2\text{ g} \), and \( 0.301\text{ g} \). What is their total combined mass reported to the proper precision?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass 1: \( 436.32\text{ g} \) (2 decimal places).
Mass 2: \( 227.2\text{ g} \) (1 decimal place).
Mass 3: \( 0.301\text{ g} \) (3 decimal places).

Step 2: Addition Rule for Significant Figures
In addition or subtraction, the final result should retain as many decimal places as the input number with the least decimal places (here, 1 decimal place from \( 227.2\text{ g} \)).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Total mass: \[ M = m_1 + m_2 + m_3 \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Arithmetic sum: \[ M = 436.32 + 227.2 + 0.301 = 663.821\text{ g} \] Rounding to 1 decimal place (the digit after 8 is 2, so 8 is unchanged): \[ M = 663.8\text{ g} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The final value is properly rounded to 1 decimal place, giving \( 663.8\text{ g} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q10 - Calculation of one light year distance value

questiontext.text: If the speed of light in vacuum is taken as \( 3.00 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1} \) and one tropical year (\( 365.25\text{ d} \)) contains \( 3.1557 \times 10^7\text{ s} \), what is the value of one light year to the appropriate number of significant figures?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Speed of light: \( c = 3.00 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1} \) (3 significant figures).
Time in one year: \( t = 3.1557 \times 10^7\text{ s} \) (5 significant figures).

Step 2: Multiplication Rule for Significant Figures
The product must retain the same number of significant figures as the least precise factor, which is 3 significant figures.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Distance of one light year: \[ d = c \times t \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Multiply the quantities: \[ d = (3.00 \times 10^8) \times (3.1557 \times 10^7)\text{ m} = 9.4671 \times 10^{15}\text{ m} \] Rounding to 3 significant figures (the fourth digit is 7, so 6 is increased to 7): \[ d = 9.47 \times 10^{15}\text{ m} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units check: \( \text{m s}^{-1} \times \text{s} = \text{m} \). The light year is \( 9.47 \times 10^{15}\text{ m} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q11 - Density of lead in SI units calculation

questiontext.text: The relative density of lead is \( 11.3 \). What is its density expressed in SI units (\( \text{kg m}^{-3} \))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Relative density of lead: \( \text{RD} = 11.3 \).

Step 2: Reference Standard Density
Relative density is the ratio of the density of the substance to the density of water at \( 4^\circ\text{C} \).
Density of water in SI units is: \[ \rho_{\text{water}} = 1.00 \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ \rho_{\text{substance}} = \text{RD} \times \rho_{\text{water}} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values: \[ \rho_{\text{lead}} = 11.3 \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3} = 1.13 \times 10^4\text{ kg m}^{-3} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( \text{kg m}^{-3} \). The density of lead is \( 1.13 \times 10^4\text{ kg m}^{-3} \) (or \( 11300\text{ kg m}^{-3} \)).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q12 - Conversion of gravitational constant to CGS units

questiontext.text: The universal gravitational constant is \( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11}\text{ N m}^2\text{ kg}^{-2} \). What is its numerical value in CGS units (\( \text{cm}^3\text{ s}^{-2}\text{ g}^{-1} \))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
\( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11}\text{ N m}^2\text{ kg}^{-2} \).

Step 2: Base Unit Conversion
Since \( 1\text{ N} = 1\text{ kg m s}^{-2} \): \[ \text{SI unit} = \text{kg m s}^{-2} \cdot \text{m}^2 \cdot \text{kg}^{-2} = \text{m}^3\text{ s}^{-2}\text{ kg}^{-1} \] Convert to CGS: \[ 1\text{ m} = 10^2\text{ cm} \implies 1\text{ m}^3 = 10^6\text{ cm}^3 \] \[ 1\text{ kg} = 10^3\text{ g} \implies 1\text{ kg}^{-1} = 10^{-3}\text{ g}^{-1} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ 1\text{ m}^3\text{ s}^{-2}\text{ kg}^{-1} = 10^6 \times 10^{-3}\text{ cm}^3\text{ s}^{-2}\text{ g}^{-1} = 10^3\text{ cm}^3\text{ s}^{-2}\text{ g}^{-1} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Multiply the SI numerical value by \( 10^3 \): \[ G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 10^3\text{ cm}^3\text{ s}^{-2}\text{ g}^{-1} = 6.67 \times 10^{-8}\text{ cm}^3\text{ s}^{-2}\text{ g}^{-1} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking dimensions: \( [\text{M}^{-1} \text{L}^3 \text{T}^{-2}] \). The value is \( 6.67 \times 10^{-8}\text{ cm}^3\text{ s}^{-2}\text{ g}^{-1} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q13 - Order of magnitude difference Earth and atom

questiontext.text: The diameter of the Earth is \( 1.28 \times 10^7\text{ m} \) and the diameter of a hydrogen atom is \( 1.06 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m} \). By how many orders of magnitude is the Earth larger than the hydrogen atom?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Diameter of the Earth: \( D_E = 1.28 \times 10^7\text{ m} \).
Diameter of the hydrogen atom: \( d_H = 1.06 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m} \).

Step 2: Order of Magnitude Convention
For a number \( a \times 10^b \): if \( a \le 5 \), the order of magnitude is \( b \); if \( 5 < a \le 10 \), the order of magnitude is \( b + 1 \).
Here \( 1.28 \le 5 \), so the order of magnitude for the Earth is \( 7 \).
For the hydrogen atom, \( 1.06 \le 5 \), so the order of magnitude is \( -10 \).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Difference in orders of magnitude: \[ \Delta b = b_E - b_H \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[ \Delta b = 7 - (-10) = 7 + 10 = 17 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The diameter of the Earth is 17 orders of magnitude larger than that of the hydrogen atom.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q14 - Estimation of hair thickness using microscope magnification

questiontext.text: A student observes the width of a human hair under a microscope of magnification \( 100 \). Over 20 observations, the average width seen in the field of view is \( 3.5\text{ mm} \). What is the estimated actual thickness of the hair?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Microscope magnification: \( M = 100 \).
Observed image width: \( w_{\text{obs}} = 3.5\text{ mm} \).

Step 2: Definition of Magnification
Linear magnification is defined as: \[ M = \frac{\text{Observed size}}{\text{Actual size}} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ \text{Actual thickness } t = \frac{w_{\text{obs}}}{M} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Divide the observed width by the magnification: \[ t = \frac{3.5\text{ mm}}{100} = 0.035\text{ mm} = 3.5 \times 10^{-2}\text{ mm} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
In metres, \( 0.035 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m} = 3.5 \times 10^{-5}\text{ m} \), which is physically plausible for human hair. The estimated thickness is \( 0.035\text{ mm} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q15 - Relative percentage error comparison of two masses

questiontext.text: Two mass measurements are taken with the same absolute error of \( \pm 0.01\text{ g} \). The first measurement is \( 1.02\text{ g} \) and the second is \( 9.89\text{ g} \). What are the relative percentage errors in the first and second measurements respectively?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Measurement 1: \( m_1 = 1.02\text{ g} \), \( \Delta m = \pm 0.01\text{ g} \).
Measurement 2: \( m_2 = 9.89\text{ g} \), \( \Delta m = \pm 0.01\text{ g} \).

Step 2: Formula for Relative Percentage Error
\[ \text{Relative error} = \left(\frac{\Delta m}{m}\right) \times 100\% \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Compute the percentage error for each value independently.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
For \( 1.02\text{ g} \): \[ \frac{\pm 0.01}{1.02} \times 100\% = \pm 0.98\% \approx \pm 1\% \] For \( 9.89\text{ g} \): \[ \frac{\pm 0.01}{9.89} \times 100\% = \pm 0.101\% \approx \pm 0.1\% \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The relative errors are \( \pm 1\% \) and \( \pm 0.1\% \) respectively.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q16 - Total thrust force under standard atmospheric pressure

questiontext.text: What is the total thrust force exerted on a horizontal surface of area \( 2.0\text{ m}^2 \) by standard atmospheric pressure (\( 1\text{ atm} = 101325\text{ Pa} \))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Surface area: \( A = 2.0\text{ m}^2 \).
Pressure: \( P = 101325\text{ Pa} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Principles
Pressure is uniform over the flat surface, so force equals pressure multiplied by area.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ F = P \times A \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Multiply the pressure by the area: \[ F = 101325\text{ N m}^{-2} \times 2.0\text{ m}^2 = 202650\text{ N} = 2.0265 \times 10^5\text{ N} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( \text{Pa} \cdot \text{m}^2 = \text{N} \). The thrust force is \( 2.0265 \times 10^5\text{ N} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q17 - Discrepancy caused by intermediate premature rounding

questiontext.text: The reciprocal of \( 9.58 \) is calculated. If it is prematurely rounded to 3 significant figures as \( 0.104 \), its reciprocal becomes \( 9.62 \). If instead an extra digit is retained as \( 0.1044 \), the original value \( 9.58 \) is retrieved. What is the absolute discrepancy in the retrieved value caused by premature rounding?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Original value: \( x = 9.58 \).
Prematurely rounded reciprocal: \( y_1 = 0.104 \).
Retrieved value from \( y_1 \): \( x_1 = \frac{1}{0.104} \approx 9.615 \approx 9.62 \).
Correctly retrieved value: \( x_2 = 9.58 \).

Step 2: Relevant Principles
Rounding error in multi-step calculations causes deviation from the true original value.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Absolute discrepancy: \[ \Delta x = |x_1 - x_2| \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Subtract the original value from the prematurely rounded result: \[ \Delta x = 9.62 - 9.58 = 0.04 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The discrepancy between the two outcomes is \( 0.04 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q18 - Conversion of acceleration into kilometer hour units

questiontext.text: An acceleration of \( 3.0\text{ m s}^{-2} \) is expressed in \( \text{km h}^{-2} \). What is its value?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Acceleration: \( a = 3.0\text{ m s}^{-2} \).

Step 2: Conversion Factors
\[ 1\text{ m} = 10^{-3}\text{ km} \] \[ 1\text{ s} = \frac{1}{3600}\text{ h} \implies 1\text{ s}^{-2} = (3600)^2\text{ h}^{-2} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ a(\text{km h}^{-2}) = a(\text{m s}^{-2}) \times 10^{-3} \times (3600)^2 \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate \( (3600)^2 \): \[ (3600)^2 = 1.296 \times 10^7 \] Substitute: \[ a = 3.0 \times 10^{-3} \times (1.296 \times 10^7)\text{ km h}^{-2} = 3.0 \times 12960 = 38880\text{ km h}^{-2} \] Rounding to 2 significant figures: \[ a \approx 3.9 \times 10^4\text{ km h}^{-2} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( \text{km h}^{-2} \). The value is \( 3.9 \times 10^4\text{ km h}^{-2} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q19 - Solid angle intercepted on a spherical surface

questiontext.text: A spherical surface intercepts an area of \( \mathrm{d}A = 0.072\text{ m}^2 \) at a distance of \( r = 0.60\text{ m} \) from the apex centre. What solid angle \( \mathrm{d}\Omega \) is subtended at the centre?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Intercepted area: \( \mathrm{d}A = 0.072\text{ m}^2 \).
Radius: \( r = 0.60\text{ m} \).

Step 2: Definition of Solid Angle
Solid angle \( \mathrm{d}\Omega \) is the ratio of intercepted spherical area to the square of radius: \[ \mathrm{d}\Omega = \frac{\mathrm{d}A}{r^2} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ r^2 = (0.60\text{ m})^2 = 0.36\text{ m}^2 \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Divide the area by the squared radius: \[ \mathrm{d}\Omega = \frac{0.072\text{ m}^2}{0.36\text{ m}^2} = 0.20\text{ sr} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units check: \( \text{m}^2 / \text{m}^2 = \text{steradian} \) (\( \text{sr} \)). The solid angle is \( 0.20\text{ sr} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q20 - Conversion of one metre into light years

questiontext.text: Given that one light year is equal to \( 9.47 \times 10^{15}\text{ m} \), what is the value of \( 1\text{ m} \) expressed in light years?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
\( 1\text{ ly} = 9.47 \times 10^{15}\text{ m} \).

Step 2: Conversion Principle
To find the number of light years in \( 1\text{ m} \), take the reciprocal of the light year in metres.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ 1\text{ m} = \frac{1}{9.47 \times 10^{15}}\text{ ly} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Divide 1 by \( 9.47 \): \[ \frac{1}{9.47} \approx 0.105597 \approx 1.056 \times 10^{-1} \] Combining with the power of 10: \[ 1\text{ m} = (1.056 \times 10^{-1}) \times 10^{-15}\text{ ly} \approx 1.06 \times 10^{-16}\text{ ly} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking magnitude: \( 1\text{ m} \) is an extremely tiny fraction of a light year (\( \approx 10^{-16}\text{ ly} \)). The value is \( 1.06 \times 10^{-16}\text{ ly} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q21 - Land area conversion into hectare unit value

questiontext.text: A rectangular plot of land has dimensions of \( 250\text{ m} \) by \( 400\text{ m} \). What is the area of this plot in hectares (\( \text{ha} \))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Length: \( l = 400\text{ m} \).
Breadth: \( b = 250\text{ m} \).

Step 2: Definitions of Area and Hectare
Area in square metres: \[ A = l \times b \] By definition: \[ 1\text{ ha} = 10^4\text{ m}^2 \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ A(\text{ha}) = \frac{A(\text{m}^2)}{10^4\text{ m}^2/\text{ha}} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate area in square metres: \[ A = 250\text{ m} \times 400\text{ m} = 100000\text{ m}^2 = 10^5\text{ m}^2 \] Convert to hectares: \[ A = \frac{10^5\text{ m}^2}{10^4\text{ m}^2/\text{ha}} = 10\text{ ha} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( \text{m}^2 / (\text{m}^2/\text{ha}) = \text{ha} \). The plot area is \( 10\text{ ha} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q22 - Pressure conversion from bar into pascals

questiontext.text: The pressure inside an industrial autoclave is measured to be \( 3.5\text{ bar} \). What is this pressure expressed in pascals (\( \text{Pa} \))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Pressure: \( P = 3.5\text{ bar} \).

Step 2: Unit Definition
As given in the standard units table: \[ 1\text{ bar} = 0.1\text{ MPa} = 10^5\text{ Pa} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ P(\text{Pa}) = P(\text{bar}) \times 10^5\text{ Pa/bar} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the measured pressure: \[ P = 3.5 \times 10^5\text{ Pa} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( \text{bar} \times \frac{\text{Pa}}{\text{bar}} = \text{Pa} \). The pressure is \( 3.5 \times 10^5\text{ Pa} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q23 - Subtraction precision with differing significant figures

questiontext.text: Two measured masses, \( 12.9\text{ g} \) (three significant figures) and \( 7.06\text{ g} \) (three significant figures), are subtracted. What is the proper value of their difference adhering to the rules of arithmetic operations?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass 1: \( 12.9\text{ g} \) (1 decimal place).
Mass 2: \( 7.06\text{ g} \) (2 decimal places).

Step 2: Subtraction Rule for Significant Figures
In subtraction, the result must retain as many decimal places as the number with the least decimal places (1 decimal place from \( 12.9\text{ g} \)), regardless of the total number of significant figures in the input values.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ \Delta m = m_1 - m_2 \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Subtract the values arithmetically: \[ \Delta m = 12.9\text{ g} - 7.06\text{ g} = 5.84\text{ g} \] Round to 1 decimal place (the digit 4 is less than 5, so 8 is unchanged): \[ \Delta m = 5.8\text{ g} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The correct reported difference is \( 5.8\text{ g} \) (which has 2 significant figures).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q24 - Total surface area and volume of measured cube

questiontext.text: Each side of a cube is measured to be \( 7.203\text{ m} \). What are the total surface area and the volume of the cube to appropriate significant figures?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Side length of the cube: \( a = 7.203\text{ m} \) (4 significant figures).

Step 2: Assumptions and Number of Significant Figures
In multiplication and exponentiation, the result must retain 4 significant figures, as the side length has 4 significant figures and 6 is an exact number.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Surface area: \[ S = 6 a^2 \] Volume: \[ V = a^3 \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
1. Calculate surface area: \[ a^2 = (7.203)^2 = 51.883209\text{ m}^2 \] \[ S = 6 \times 51.883209 = 311.299254\text{ m}^2 \] Rounding to 4 significant figures: \[ S = 311.3\text{ m}^2 \] 2. Calculate volume: \[ V = (7.203)^3 = 373.714754\dots\text{ m}^3 \] Rounding to 4 significant figures: \[ V = 373.7\text{ m}^3 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The surface area is \( 311.3\text{ m}^2 \) and the volume is \( 373.7\text{ m}^3 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q25 - Uncertainty evaluation in rectangular sheet area calculation

questiontext.text: The length and breadth of a thin rectangular sheet are measured using a metre scale as \( 16.2 \pm 0.1\text{ cm} \) and \( 10.1 \pm 0.1\text{ cm} \). What is the area of the sheet quoted with its uncertainty?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Length: \( l = 16.2 \pm 0.1\text{ cm} \).
Breadth: \( b = 10.1 \pm 0.1\text{ cm} \).

Step 2: Error Propagation Rules
When two quantities multiply, their relative fractional errors add: \[ \frac{\Delta A}{A} = \frac{\Delta l}{l} + \frac{\Delta b}{b} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Area: \( A = l \times b \).
Absolute uncertainty: \( \Delta A = A \times \left(\frac{\Delta A}{A}\right) \).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Relative errors: \[ \frac{\Delta l}{l} = \frac{0.1}{16.2} \approx 0.00617 = 0.6\% \] \[ \frac{\Delta b}{b} = \frac{0.1}{10.1} \approx 0.00990 = 1.0\% \] Combined relative error: \[ \frac{\Delta A}{A} = 0.6\% + 1.0\% = 1.6\% \] Calculated area: \[ A = 16.2 \times 10.1 = 163.62\text{ cm}^2 \] Absolute error: \[ \Delta A = 163.62 \times 0.016 = 2.618\text{ cm}^2 \approx 3\text{ cm}^2 \] Rounding area to be consistent with uncertainty: \[ A = 164 \pm 3\text{ cm}^2 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The area quoted with proper uncertainty is \( 164 \pm 3\text{ cm}^2 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q26 - Total mass and difference of added gold pieces

questiontext.text: The mass of a box measured by a grocer balance is \( 2.30\text{ kg} \). Two gold pieces of masses \( 20.15\text{ g} \) and \( 20.17\text{ g} \) are added to the box. What are the total mass of the box and the difference in the masses of the pieces to correct significant figures?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of box: \( m_0 = 2.30\text{ kg} \) (known to 2 decimal places in kg).
Mass of gold piece 1: \( m_1 = 20.15\text{ g} = 0.02015\text{ kg} \).
Mass of gold piece 2: \( m_2 = 20.17\text{ g} = 0.02017\text{ kg} \).

Step 2: Decimal Place Consistency Principle
In addition, the result cannot have more decimal places than the least precise measurement (\( 2.30\text{ kg} \), having 2 decimal places). In subtraction of the two pieces, both are measured to 2 decimal places in grams.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Total mass: \( M = m_0 + m_1 + m_2 \).
Mass difference: \( \Delta m = m_2 - m_1 \).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Total mass: \[ M = 2.30\text{ kg} + 0.02015\text{ kg} + 0.02017\text{ kg} = 2.34032\text{ kg} \] Rounding to 2 decimal places: \[ M = 2.34\text{ kg} \] Difference in mass of pieces: \[ \Delta m = 20.17\text{ g} - 20.15\text{ g} = 0.02\text{ g} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The total mass of the box is \( 2.34\text{ kg} \) and the difference in the masses is \( 0.02\text{ g} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q27 - Calorie value in arbitrary defined base units

questiontext.text: A calorie equals \( 4.2\text{ J} \) where \( 1\text{ J} = 1\text{ kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-2} \). Suppose a new system of units is employed where the unit of mass is \( \alpha\text{ kg} \), the unit of length is \( \beta\text{ m} \), and the unit of time is \( \gamma\text{ s} \). What is the magnitude of one calorie in the new system of units?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Energy: \( E = 4.2\text{ J} = 4.2\text{ kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-2} \).
SI base units: \( M_1 = 1\text{ kg} \), \( L_1 = 1\text{ m} \), \( T_1 = 1\text{ s} \), with numerical value \( n_1 = 4.2 \).
New base units: \( M_2 = \alpha\text{ kg} \), \( L_2 = \beta\text{ m} \), \( T_2 = \gamma\text{ s} \).

Step 2: Dimensional Formula of Energy
\[ [E] = [\text{M}^a \text{L}^b \text{T}^c] = [\text{M}^1 \text{L}^2 \text{T}^{-2}] \] where \( a = 1 \), \( b = 2 \), \( c = -2 \).

Step 3: Unit Conversion Formula
\[ n_2 = n_1 \left[\frac{M_1}{M_2}\right]^a \left[\frac{L_1}{L_2}\right]^b \left[\frac{T_1}{T_2}\right]^c \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values: \[ n_2 = 4.2 \left[\frac{1\text{ kg}}{\alpha\text{ kg}}\right]^1 \left[\frac{1\text{ m}}{\beta\text{ m}}\right]^2 \left[\frac{1\text{ s}}{\gamma\text{ s}}\right]^{-2} \] \[ n_2 = 4.2 \left(\alpha^{-1}\right) \left(\beta^{-2}\right) \left(\gamma^2\right) = 4.2 \, \alpha^{-1} \beta^{-2} \gamma^2 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Dimensions check: mass power \( -1 \), length power \( -2 \), time power \( 2 \). The magnitude is \( 4.2 \, \alpha^{-1} \beta^{-2} \gamma^2 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q28 - Sun Earth distance in unit light speed

questiontext.text: A new unit of length is chosen such that the speed of light in vacuum is unity (\( c = 1 \)). What is the distance between the Sun and the Earth in terms of this new unit if light takes \( 8\text{ min} \) and \( 20\text{ s} \) to cover this distance?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Speed of light in the new unit: \( c = 1\text{ new unit s}^{-1} \).
Time of travel: \( t = 8\text{ min} + 20\text{ s} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Unit Conversion
Convert the total time into seconds: \[ t = (8 \times 60) + 20 = 480 + 20 = 500\text{ s} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[ \text{Distance } d = c \times t \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Multiply speed by time: \[ d = 1\text{ new unit s}^{-1} \times 500\text{ s} = 500\text{ new units} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The distance between the Sun and the Earth is \( 500\text{ new units} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q29 - Linear magnification from projected slide area ratio

questiontext.text: The photograph of a house occupies an area of \( 1.75\text{ cm}^2 \) on a slide. The slide is projected onto a screen, and the area of the house on the screen is \( 1.55\text{ m}^2 \). What is the linear magnification of the projector-screen arrangement?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Object area on slide: \( A_1 = 1.75\text{ cm}^2 \).
Image area on screen: \( A_2 = 1.55\text{ m}^2 \).

Step 2: Relation Between Linear and Areal Magnification
Areal magnification is the ratio of image area to object area: \[ m_{\text{area}} = \frac{A_2}{A_1} \] Linear magnification \( m \) is the square root of areal magnification: \[ m = \sqrt{m_{\text{area}}} \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Convert \( A_2 \) to \( \text{cm}^2 \): \[ 1\text{ m}^2 = 10^4\text{ cm}^2 \implies A_2 = 1.55 \times 10^4\text{ cm}^2 = 15500\text{ cm}^2 \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Compute areal magnification: \[ m_{\text{area}} = \frac{15500\text{ cm}^2}{1.75\text{ cm}^2} \approx 8857.14 \] Take square root: \[ m = \sqrt{8857.14} \approx 94.11 \] Rounding to 3 significant figures: \[ m = 94.1 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: dimensionless ratio. The linear magnification is \( 94.1 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q30 - Surface area and volume of thin metal sheet

questiontext.text: The length, breadth, and thickness of a rectangular sheet of metal are \( 4.234\text{ m} \), \( 1.005\text{ m} \), and \( 2.01\text{ cm} \) respectively. What are the total surface area and volume of the sheet to the correct significant figures?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Length: \( l = 4.234\text{ m} \) (4 significant figures).
Breadth: \( b = 1.005\text{ m} \) (4 significant figures).
Thickness: \( t = 2.01\text{ cm} = 0.0201\text{ m} \) (3 significant figures).

Step 2: Significant Figures Constraint
Because the thickness has 3 significant figures, the calculated total surface area and volume must be rounded to 3 significant figures.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Total surface area: \[ A = 2(l b + b t + t l) \] Volume: \[ V = l \times b \times t \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
1. Area calculation: \[ l b = 4.234 \times 1.005 = 4.25517\text{ m}^2 \] \[ b t = 1.005 \times 0.0201 = 0.0202005\text{ m}^2 \] \[ t l = 0.0201 \times 4.234 = 0.0851034\text{ m}^2 \] Sum of three face areas: \[ 4.25517 + 0.02020 + 0.08510 = 4.36047\text{ m}^2 \] Total area: \[ A = 2 \times 4.36047 = 8.72094\text{ m}^2 \approx 8.72\text{ m}^2 \] 2. Volume calculation: \[ V = 4.234 \times 1.005 \times 0.0201\text{ m}^3 = 0.0855289\dots\text{ m}^3 \] Rounding to 3 significant figures: \[ V = 0.0855\text{ m}^3 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The total surface area is \( 8.72\text{ m}^2 \) and the volume is \( 0.0855\text{ m}^3 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q31 - Atomic volume of one mole of hydrogen atoms

questiontext.text: The atomic radius of a hydrogen atom is approximately \( 0.5\text{ \AA} = 0.5 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m} \). Taking Avogadro number as \( N_{\text{A}} = 6.02 \times 10^{23}\text{ mol}^{-1} \), what is the total atomic volume occupied by one mole of hydrogen atoms?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Radius of single atom: \( r = 0.5 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m} \).
Avogadro constant: \( N_{\text{A}} = 6.02 \times 10^{23}\text{ mol}^{-1} \).

Step 2: Assumptions of Spherical Model
Each hydrogen atom is assumed to be a sphere of radius \( r \).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Volume of a single spherical atom: \[ V_{\text{atom}} = \frac{4}{3} \pi r^3 \] Total atomic volume of one mole: \[ V_{\text{total}} = N_{\text{A}} \times V_{\text{atom}} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate \( r^3 \): \[ r^3 = (0.5 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m})^3 = 0.125 \times 10^{-30}\text{ m}^3 \] Single atom volume: \[ V_{\text{atom}} = \frac{4}{3} \times 3.1416 \times 0.125 \times 10^{-30} \approx 5.236 \times 10^{-31}\text{ m}^3 \] Total volume for one mole: \[ V_{\text{total}} = (6.02 \times 10^{23}) \times (5.236 \times 10^{-31}\text{ m}^3) \approx 3.15 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}^3 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( \text{m}^3 \). The total atomic volume is approximately \( 3.15 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}^3 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q32 - Molar to atomic volume ratio of hydrogen gas

questiontext.text: One mole of an ideal gas at standard temperature and pressure occupies a molar volume of \( 22.4\text{ L} \). Taking the total atomic volume of one mole of hydrogen atoms as \( 3.15 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}^3 \), what is the ratio of the molar volume to the atomic volume?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Molar volume: \( V_m = 22.4\text{ L} \).
Total atomic volume: \( V_{\text{atomic}} = 3.15 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}^3 \).

Step 2: Unit Conversion
Convert litres to cubic metres: \[ V_m = 22.4\text{ L} = 22.4 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^3 \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Ratio: \[ R = \frac{V_m}{V_{\text{atomic}}} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values: \[ R = \frac{22.4 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^3}{3.15 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}^3} \] \[ R = \frac{22.4}{3.15} \times 10^4 \approx 7.11 \times 10^4 \approx 7.1 \times 10^4 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The ratio is dimensionless and on the order of \( 10^4 \text{ to } 10^5 \), reflecting the vast intermolecular space in a gas. The ratio is approximately \( 7.1 \times 10^4 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q33 - Average mass density calculation for the Sun

questiontext.text: Given that the mass of the Sun is \( 2.0 \times 10^{30}\text{ kg} \) and its radius is \( 7.0 \times 10^8\text{ m} \), calculate the average mass density of the Sun.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of the Sun: \( M = 2.0 \times 10^{30}\text{ kg} \).
Radius of the Sun: \( R = 7.0 \times 10^8\text{ m} \).

Step 2: Spherical Geometry Model
The Sun is modelled as a sphere of radius \( R \).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Volume: \[ V = \frac{4}{3} \pi R^3 \] Average density: \[ \rho = \frac{M}{V} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate \( R^3 \): \[ R^3 = (7.0 \times 10^8\text{ m})^3 = 343 \times 10^{24}\text{ m}^3 \] Calculate volume: \[ V = \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 343 \times 10^{24}\text{ m}^3 = \frac{4312}{3} \times 10^{24}\text{ m}^3 \approx 1.437 \times 10^{27}\text{ m}^3 \] Calculate density: \[ \rho = \frac{2.0 \times 10^{30}\text{ kg}}{1.437 \times 10^{27}\text{ m}^3} \approx 1.39 \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3} \approx 1.4 \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( \text{kg m}^{-3} \). The density is approximately \( 1.4 \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_SEQUENCING_Q01 - Logical sequence of dimensional analysis method

questiontext.text:
The following steps are involved in deducing a mathematical relationship among interdependent physical quantities using the method of dimensional analysis:

  1. Equate the exponents of the base dimensions \([M]\), \([L]\), and \([T]\) on both sides of the equation using the principle of homogeneity.
  2. Express the dependent physical quantity as proportional to the product of powers of the independent physical quantities with undetermined exponents.
  3. Substitute the determined values of the exponents back into the original product form to obtain the final formula.
  4. Substitute the dimensional formula of each physical quantity on both sides of the equation.
  5. Solve the resulting system of simultaneous algebraic equations to find the values of the undetermined exponents.

Which of the following represents the correct logical sequence of these steps?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Deducing a relation among physical quantities using dimensional analysis relies on expressing the target quantity as a product of powers of the variables it depends upon, followed by the application of the principle of homogeneity of dimensions, which states that the dimensions of base quantities on both sides of a physical equation must be identical.

Step 2: Logical Sequence of the Derivation Process
The systematic procedure follows these stages:
First, the dependence of the physical quantity on up to three independent variables is formulated as a product with undetermined exponents, introducing a dimensionless constant of proportionality.
Second, the dimensional formulae of the dependent quantity and all independent quantities are substituted on both sides of the expression.
Third, by the principle of homogeneity of dimensions, the exponents of the fundamental dimensions \([M]\), \([L]\), and \([T]\) on the left-hand side are equated to the corresponding exponents on the right-hand side.
Fourth, the resulting simultaneous linear algebraic equations are solved to determine the numerical values of the unknown exponents.
Fifth, the evaluated exponents are substituted back into the initial product equation to arrive at the final dimensional relation.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct chronological and logical sequence begins with formulating the product dependence with unknown exponents, followed by substituting the dimensional formulae on both sides, equating the powers of the base dimensions using the principle of homogeneity, solving the resulting system of algebraic equations for the exponents, and finally substituting the exponents back into the initial relation.
Thus, the correct sequence is: (II) \(\rightarrow\) (IV) \(\rightarrow\) (I) \(\rightarrow\) (V) \(\rightarrow\) (III).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q01 - SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature

questiontext.text: Which of the following represents the SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature along with its standard symbol?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In the International System of Units (SI), seven fundamental physical quantities are chosen as base quantities, each having an internationally accepted base unit and symbol defined by the General Conference on Weights and Measures (CGPM).

Step 2: Identification of Base Unit and Symbol
According to the SI base unit definitions, the unit of thermodynamic temperature is the kelvin, denoted by the standard uppercase symbol \( \text{K} \). Other temperature units such as degree Celsius (\( ^\circ\text{C} \)) or degree Fahrenheit (\( ^\circ\text{F} \)) are derived or non-SI units.

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature is the kelvin with the symbol \( \text{K} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q02 - Defining physical constant for kilogram unit

questiontext.text: In the revised International System of Units (SI) adopted by the General Conference on Weights and Measures, the kilogram is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of which fundamental physical constant?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The SI base units were revised in November 2018 so that each base unit is defined in terms of a fixed numerical value of an invariant fundamental constant of nature.

Step 2: Analysis of the Kilogram Definition
The kilogram, symbol \( \text{kg} \), is the SI unit of mass. It is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the Planck constant \( h \) to be \( 6.62607015 \times 10^{-34} \) when expressed in the unit \( \text{J s} \), which is equal to \( \text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-1} \), where the metre and the second are defined in terms of the speed of light \( c \) and the caesium frequency \( \Delta \nu_{\text{Cs}} \).

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The defining fundamental physical constant for the kilogram is the Planck constant \( h \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q03 - Atomic standard defining the SI second

questiontext.text: The SI base unit of time, the second (\( \text{s} \)), is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the unperturbed ground-state hyperfine transition frequency of which atom?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The standard unit of time is defined using a highly stable and reproducible atomic transition frequency.

Step 2: Identification of the Standard Nucliude
The second is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the caesium frequency \( \Delta \nu_{\text{Cs}} \), the unperturbed ground-state hyperfine transition frequency of the caesium-133 atom, to be \( 9192631770 \) when expressed in the unit \( \text{Hz} \), which is equal to \( \text{s}^{-1} \).

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The atomic standard used to define the second is the caesium-133 atom.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q04 - Defining physical constant for the ampere

questiontext.text: In the revised SI definitions, the ampere (\( \text{A} \)) is defined by fixing the numerical value of which constant?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The SI unit of electric current, the ampere, was redefined in terms of the fundamental electric charge carried by a single proton or electron.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Defining Constant
The ampere, symbol \( \text{A} \), is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the elementary charge \( e \) to be \( 1.602176634 \times 10^{-19} \) when expressed in the unit \( \text{C} \), which is equal to \( \text{A s} \), where the second is defined in terms of the caesium hyperfine frequency.

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The fundamental constant used to define the ampere is the elementary charge \( e \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q05 - Nature of supplementary plane and solid angles

questiontext.text: In the International System of Units, plane angle and solid angle are physical quantities that have:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Plane angle is defined as the ratio of arc length to radius (\( \mathrm{d}\theta = \mathrm{d}s / r \)), and solid angle is defined as the ratio of intercepted area to the square of radius (\( \mathrm{d}\Omega = \mathrm{d}A / r^2 \)).

Step 2: Dimensional and Unit Analysis
Because plane angle is a ratio of length to length, its dimensional formula is \( [\text{L}] / [\text{L}] = [\text{M}^0 \text{L}^0 \text{T}^0] \). Because solid angle is a ratio of area to the square of length, its dimensional formula is \( [\text{L}^2] / [\text{L}^2] = [\text{M}^0 \text{L}^0 \text{T}^0] \). Hence, both quantities are dimensionless. However, they are assigned standard SI units: the radian (\( \text{rad} \)) for plane angle and the steradian (\( \text{sr} \)) for solid angle.

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
Both plane angle and solid angle have units but no dimensions.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q06 - Solid angle calculation for spherical cap

questiontext.text:
A spherical surface intercepts an area of \( 0.048\text{ m}^2 \) at a radial distance of \( 0.40\text{ m} \) from the apex center \( \text{O} \), as illustrated in the schematic below:

What is the solid angle \( \mathrm{d}\Omega \) subtended by this surface area at the apex?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Intercepted spherical area \( \mathrm{d}A = 0.048\text{ m}^2 \).
Radius from the apex \( r = 0.40\text{ m} \).

Step 2: Relevant Formula
By definition, the solid angle \( \mathrm{d}\Omega \) subtended by an intercepted area \( \mathrm{d}A \) of a spherical surface of radius \( r \) is given by: \[ \mathrm{d}\Omega = \frac{\mathrm{d}A}{r^2} \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Working
First, calculate the square of the radius: \[ r^2 = (0.40\text{ m})^2 = 0.16\text{ m}^2 \] Next, divide the intercepted surface area by the squared radius: \[ \mathrm{d}\Omega = \frac{0.048\text{ m}^2}{0.16\text{ m}^2} = 0.30\text{ sr} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The ratio has dimensions of area over area, resulting in the dimensionless unit steradian (\( \text{sr} \)). The calculated solid angle is \( 0.30\text{ sr} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q07 - Definition of mole and elementary entities

questiontext.text: According to the SI definition of the base unit mole, which condition must always be fulfilled when using the mole to state an amount of substance?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The mole is the SI base unit of amount of substance (\( n \)). One mole contains exactly \( 6.02214076 \times 10^{23} \) elementary entities, which is the fixed numerical value of the Avogadro constant \( N_{\text{A}} \).

Step 2: Specification Requirement
Because amount of substance is a count of entities, the SI definition explicitly requires that the elementary entities must be specified. These entities may be atoms, molecules, ions, electrons, other particles, or specified groups of such particles.

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The elementary entities must be explicitly specified (such as atoms, molecules, ions, or electrons).

answer.text: The measurement must only be performed on pure solid elements
The elementary entities (such as atoms, molecules, or ions) must be explicitly specified
The mass of the substance must be exactly equal to 12 grams
The substance must be an ideal gas at standard temperature and pressure

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q08 - Conversion of hectare into SI units

questiontext.text: The unit 'hectare' (symbol \( \text{ha} \)) is retained for general use to measure land area. What is its exact equivalent value in SI base units?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The hectare is defined based on the hectometre (\( \text{hm} \)), where \( 1\text{ hm} = 100\text{ m} = 10^2\text{ m} \).

Step 2: Calculation of Equivalent Area
One hectare is the area of a square with sides of length \( 1\text{ hm} \): \[ 1\text{ ha} = 1\text{ hm}^2 = (10^2\text{ m})^2 = 10^4\text{ m}^2 \]

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The equivalent value of 1 hectare in SI units is \( 10^4\text{ m}^2 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q09 - Standard atmospheric pressure in pascals

questiontext.text: What is the exact equivalent value of one standard atmospheric pressure (\( 1\text{ atm} \)) expressed in pascals (\( \text{Pa} \))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Standard atmospheric pressure is a conventional reference unit of pressure retained for general scientific and engineering usage.

Step 2: SI Value Identification
According to the standard conversion table for units retained for general use, standard atmospheric pressure is defined as: \[ 1\text{ atm} = 101325\text{ Pa} = 1.01325 \times 10^5\text{ Pa} \approx 1.013 \times 10^5\text{ Pa} \]

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The value of one standard atmospheric pressure is \( 101325\text{ Pa} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q10 - Relationship between bar and pascal units

questiontext.text: The unit 'bar' is widely used in meteorology and fluid mechanics for pressure. In terms of the SI unit pascal (\( \text{Pa} \)), \( 1\text{ bar} \) is equal to:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The bar is a metric unit of pressure, though not part of the official SI system, retained for general use.

Step 2: Value in SI Units
As given in the standard table of units retained for general use, one bar is defined as: \[ 1\text{ bar} = 0.1\text{ MPa} = 10^5\text{ Pa} \]

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
One bar is exactly equal to \( 10^5\text{ Pa} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q11 - Value of mass unit carat in milligrams

questiontext.text: The unit 'carat' (symbol \( \text{c} \)), commonly used in commercial trade of gemstones, is equivalent to which mass in milligrams?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The carat is a traditional unit of mass retained for general commercial use, especially for diamonds and precious stones.

Step 2: Value in Milligrams
According to the standard unit conversion table, one carat is defined as: \[ 1\text{ carat} = 200\text{ mg} = 0.2\text{ g} = 2 \times 10^{-4}\text{ kg} \]

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The value of 1 carat is \( 200\text{ mg} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q12 - Values of quintal and tonne in kilograms

questiontext.text: In standard commercial and industrial measurements of large masses, the values of 1 quintal (\( \text{q} \)) and 1 tonne (\( \text{t} \)) expressed in kilograms are respectively:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Both the quintal and the tonne (metric ton) are non-SI units of mass retained for general use.

Step 2: Evaluation of Values
One quintal is defined as \( 1\text{ q} = 100\text{ kg} = 10^2\text{ kg} \).
One tonne is defined as \( 1\text{ t} = 1000\text{ kg} = 10^3\text{ kg} \).

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The mass of 1 quintal is \( 100\text{ kg} \) and the mass of 1 tonne is \( 1000\text{ kg} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q13 - Definition of significant figures in measurement

questiontext.text: In reporting the result of a physical measurement, the significant figures (or significant digits) are defined as:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Every physical measurement involves an experimental uncertainty determined by the least count of the measuring instrument.

Step 2: Definition of Significant Digits
By convention, the reported result of a measurement includes all digits in the number that are known reliably and with certainty, plus the first digit that is uncertain. These reliable digits plus the first uncertain digit are called significant figures.

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
Significant figures comprise all reliably known digits plus the first uncertain digit.

answer.text: All reliably known digits plus the first uncertain digit
Only the digits that are completely certain
The total number of digits displayed after the decimal point

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q14 - Invariance of significant figures under unit conversion

questiontext.text: A measured length is reported as \( 2.308\text{ cm} \). When expressed in different units, it can be written as \( 0.02308\text{ m} \), \( 23.08\text{ mm} \), or \( 23080\,\mu\text{m} \). How many significant figures do each of these numbers possess?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The precision of a measurement depends solely on the measuring instrument and cannot be altered by merely changing the units of measurement.

Step 2: Application of Significant Figure Rules
- In \( 2.308\text{ cm} \), there are four non-zero digits and an internal zero: 4 significant figures.
- In \( 0.02308\text{ m} \), the leading zeros to the left of 2 are placeholders and not significant: 4 significant figures (2, 3, 0, 8).
- In \( 23.08\text{ mm} \), there are 4 significant figures.
- In \( 23080\,\mu\text{m} \), coming from the same measurement, the trailing zero arises from unit conversion and does not represent an extra measured precision: 4 significant figures.

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
A change of units does not change the number of significant figures; all these representations have 4 significant figures.

answer.text: Different numbers of significant figures ranging from 4 to 5

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q15 - Significant figures in integers versus decimals

questiontext.text: Consider the two reported values \( 123000\text{ mm} \) and \( 0.06900\text{ g} \). How many significant figures are there in each value?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Rules for significant figures distinguish between trailing zeros in numbers without a decimal point and trailing zeros in numbers with a decimal point.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Number
1. For \( 123000\text{ mm} \): This is an integer without a decimal point. Terminal or trailing zeros in a number without a decimal point are not significant. Only the digits 1, 2, and 3 are significant, giving 3 significant figures.
2. For \( 0.06900\text{ g} \): For a number less than 1, zeros to the left of the first non-zero digit are not significant, but trailing zeros in a number with a decimal point are significant. Thus, the digits 6, 9, 0, and 0 are significant, giving 4 significant figures.

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
\( 123000\text{ mm} \) has 3 significant figures, and \( 0.06900\text{ g} \) has 4 significant figures.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q16 - Significant figures in scientific notation base

questiontext.text: A measured distance is expressed in scientific notation as \( 4.700 \times 10^3\text{ mm} \). How many significant figures does this measurement contain?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In scientific notation (\( a \times 10^b \)), the order of magnitude or power of 10 is purely an exponent indicating scale and does not contribute to the precision of measurement.

Step 2: Analysis of the Base Number
